supermarket.note: Such as Fresno chilies work well here.

tools.name: Stockpot
tools.note: Large enough to hold the chicken with room to cover it in water.

tools.name: Bowl
tools.note: Use a large bowl for the ice bath.

tools.name: Heavy-bottomed saucepan
tools.note: A medium size works best, and a lid helps the rice steam evenly.

tools.name: Saucepan
tools.note: Use a small one, for heating the oil for the ginger-scallion sauce.

tools.name: Blender
tools.note: A mini food processor can be used in its place.

tools.name: Heatproof bowl
tools.note: Use two small bowls, one for each sauce.

steps.title: Do the prep
points: Do all the prep first.
Pull the loose fat from the chicken's cavity and neck, chop it small, and set it aside for the rice.
Rub the chicken all over with 1 tablespoon of the salt, then rinse it under cold water.
Peel the ginger.
Cut half of it into thin coins and grate the other half; you need about 3 tablespoons grated.
Smash 2 of the scallions with the flat of the knife and thinly slice the other 4.
Mince all 8 garlic cloves and divide them into two piles.
Stem and roughly chop the chilies.
Rinse the rice in several changes of cold water until the water runs nearly clear, then drain it well.
Slice the cucumber into thin rounds.
Fill the large bowl with the ice and cold water.

steps.title: Poach the chicken
points: Set the chicken breast side up in the stockpot and add cold water to cover it by 1 inch.
Add the ginger coins, the smashed scallions, and 1 tablespoon of the salt.
Bring it to a boil over high heat, skim off the foam, then turn the heat down to the lowest setting so the water barely trembles.
Cover and cook for 35 to 45 minutes, until the thermometer reads 165°F in the thickest part of the thigh, not touching bone.

steps.title: Lift and chill the chicken
points: Lift the chicken out with the tongs, tilting it so the hot broth runs out of the cavity back into the pot, and lower it into the ice bath.
Leave it there for 10 minutes to firm the skin.
Keep the broth in the stockpot over low heat.

steps.title: Cook the rice
points: Put the chopped chicken fat in the medium saucepan over medium-low heat and cook for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until you have about 2 tablespoons of liquid fat.
Lift out the crisp bits and discard them.
If the fat comes to less than 2 tablespoons, make up the difference with the 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil.
Add one pile of minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant but not brown.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes to coat every grain.
Strain 2 1/2 cups of the hot broth through the sieve into the pan and add 1 teaspoon of salt.
Bring it to a boil, cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting, and cook for 15 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Make chili sauce
points: While the rice cooks, make the chili sauce.
Put the chilies, the second pile of garlic, 1 tablespoon of the grated ginger, the lime juice, the sugar, 1/2 teaspoon of salt, and 2 tablespoons of the strained broth in the blender.
Blend until fairly smooth, then scrape it into one of the small bowls.

steps.title: Make ginger-scallion sauce
points: Put the remaining 2 tablespoons of grated ginger, the sliced scallions, and the last 1/2 teaspoon of salt in the other small heatproof bowl.
Heat the 1/4 cup of vegetable oil in the small saucepan over medium heat for about 2 minutes, until it shimmers.
Pour it carefully over the ginger and scallions; it will sizzle.
Stir once.

steps.title: Dry, carve, and serve chicken
points: Take the chicken out of the ice bath, pat it dry, and rub the skin with the sesame oil.
Carve it into legs, thighs, and breasts, then cut the pieces into slices about 3/4 inch thick.
Lay them on a plate and spoon the soy sauce and 2 tablespoons of warm broth over the top.
Fluff the rice and serve it with the chicken, the cucumber, the two sauces, and small bowls of the remaining hot broth.

troubleshooting.problem: The meat near the bone is still pink and below 165°F
troubleshooting.solution: Return it to the broth at the same low heat for another 5 to 10 minutes and check again.

troubleshooting.problem: The breast meat is dry and stringy
troubleshooting.solution: The water boiled during poaching. Keep it at the lowest heat so only a few small bubbles rise, and take the chicken out as soon as it reaches temperature.

troubleshooting.problem: The rice is wet and sticky
troubleshooting.solution: Rinse until the water is nearly clear, drain it well, and measure the broth exactly.

troubleshooting.problem: The rice has scorched on the bottom
troubleshooting.solution: The heat was too high after the boil. Turn the burner to its lowest setting once the lid goes on, and use a heavy-bottomed pan.
